hero.headline: A well spring is a source that never stops giving.
hero.body: Steady. Clear. Quietly renewing. That is the kind of therapeutic care we provide — a licensed, staff-secure Level III residential treatment home where children and adolescents ages 6–17 receive individual therapy, group therapy, psychiatric medication management, and round-the-clock emotional support from licensed clinicians and trained professionals. When a child has given all they have to surviving, we give back twice over: clinical treatment, safety, healing, and the simple joy of being a kid again. Our program is intentionally small — four to six children in one household — so every child receives deeply individualized clinical attention, and every licensed therapist and direct care professional has the time to truly know them.
hero.tagline: Empowerment · Growth · Freedom · Health · Wholeness · Healing

footer.description: A licensed staff-secure Level III residential treatment facility serving children ages 6–17 in Wake County, North Carolina — where children heal, grow, and graduate toward the lives they deserve.

faqs.q: What is a staff-secure Level III residential treatment facility?
faqs.a: Level III residential treatment offers 24-hour clinical care in a structured, home-like setting for children whose behavioral and mental health needs cannot yet be safely met at home or in a less restrictive setting. Under 10A NCAC 27G .1701, a Level III Staff-Secure facility is a free-standing residential facility that provides intensive, active therapeutic treatment and interventions within a system of care approach. "Staff-secure" means staff are required to be awake during client sleep hours and supervision shall be continuous as set forth in Rule .1704. This allows children to participate in school, family visits, community activities, and therapeutic programming while receiving the intensive clinical support they need. Our program combines individual therapy, group therapy, psychiatric medication management, behavioral intervention, and psychosocial rehabilitation — all delivered by licensed clinicians within a warm, predictable daily routine.

We serve children and adolescents, ages 6–17, who have been placed out of home due to behavioral and mental health needs including trauma, severe emotional disturbance, mood disorders, anxiety, ADHD, and co-occurring conditions. Under .1701(c)–(d), eligible youth have a primary diagnosis of mental illness, emotional disturbance, or substance-related disorder, do not meet criteria for inpatient psychiatric services, and require removal from home and treatment in a staff-secure setting. Our program is intentionally small — four to six children in one household — well below the regulatory maximum of twelve children permitted under .1706(a). We have elected this lower capacity as a best-practice census ceiling to ensure every child receives deeply individualized clinical attention. A young person who turns 18 while in placement may continue in the program for up to six months or the end of the school year, whichever is longer, per .1706(e).

faqs.q: What makes Well Spring Intervention different from other residential programs?
faqs.a: Our size is our strength. With only four to six children — well below the regulatory maximum of twelve under .1706(a) — we maintain a minimum of two awake, trained professionals on duty at all times for every one to four children, a 2:4 ratio, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year. Single-staffing is prohibited at all times. Every child has a primary licensed therapist who sees them daily — not weekly, daily. Our education liaison ensures every child stays enrolled in community school, attends every IEP meeting, and receives homework support every evening. We are not an institution; we are a home. The therapeutic relationship is the foundation of everything we do — children heal in the context of safe, consistent, caring relationships with adults who keep showing up, day after day.

Most placements are coordinated through county care coordination (LME/MCOs), departments of social services, and placing agencies. The process begins with a referral — which you can submit directly through our website at wellspringintervention.com/refer. We review the child's clinical history, screen for fit, and schedule a pre-placement visit where the child and family tour the home and meet the team. We move quickly because children in transition cannot wait, but we never rush the clinical screening — we want to be sure we can genuinely help each child who comes through our door.

faqs.q: What therapeutic services does my child receive?
faqs.a: Each child receives an individualized treatment plan (ITP) built within the first 30 days, developed by a Qualified Professional in collaboration with the child, family, and care team. Per .1701(e), services include individualized supervision and structure of daily living, individual therapy (at least weekly), group therapy, family therapy sessions, psychiatric evaluation and medication management, behavioral intervention planning (BIP), case management, psychosocial rehabilitation, and life-skills coaching. Treatment is reviewed and updated every 30 days. We also provide educational support — our staff sits beside children for homework every evening, and our education liaison coordinates with the child's school and attends every IEP meeting.

faqs.q: Will my child keep going to school?
faqs.a: Yes — absolutely. Within days of arrival, our education liaison enrolls your child in a local community school and arranges transportation. We attend every IEP meeting, follow each child's education plan, track daily attendance, and sit beside them for homework every evening. Credits keep counting, friendships keep growing, and graduations stay on schedule — because therapeutic growth and educational progress go hand in hand. A child's education does not pause while they heal; it accelerates, supported by adults who care.

Yes — we believe families are partners, not visitors. Family contact through visits, calls, and family therapy sessions is part of everyday life here. Caregivers help shape every treatment plan, participate in regular Child and Family Team (CFT) meetings, and have a genuine voice in every clinical decision. Planning for home begins on day one — not the week before discharge. We know that a child's healing happens in the context of their family, and our job is to strengthen that family system, not replace it.

faqs.q: What happens when it's time to leave?
faqs.a: From day one, your child's team is planning the way home. Per .1701(e), our program supports step-down to a less intensive setting. Before any transition, we hold a pre-discharge CFT meeting and put the aftercare plan in writing — including outpatient therapy appointments, psychiatric medication management, primary care coordination, school re-entry, and any step-down services. We hand off cleanly to the receiving providers with records, recommendations, and warm introductions. And when a child completes the program, we celebrate — because leaving ready, with the tools and the support to succeed, is the goal we have been working toward together.

faqs.q: How do you keep children safe?
faqs.a: Safety is the foundation of everything we do — physical and emotional. Per .1701(b) and .1704, our facility is staff-secure, meaning trained professionals are awake and on duty 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with continuous supervision (line-of-sight or continuous auditory monitoring) of all youth at all times. We maintain a minimum of two awake staff members for every one to four children (2:4 ratio) at all times. All staff complete comprehensive training including CPR, First Aid, crisis prevention and de-escalation, trauma-informed care, medication administration, and abuse/neglect reporting before working independently with children. We conduct regular emergency drills per .1708 (fire, severe weather, lockdown), maintain locked medication storage, and follow strict safety protocols. Physical restraint is used only as a last resort when there is imminent danger, and every incident is documented and debriefed within 24 hours.

faqs.q: Is the program licensed and accredited?
faqs.a: We are licensed by the North Carolina Division of Health Service Regulation (DHSR) under 10A NCAC 27G .1700 as a Level III Residential Treatment Facility — Staff-Secure for Children and Adolescents. This is a free-standing residential facility licensed as a program setting only, not a family home. We are an in-network provider with Alliance Health (the Tailored Plan for Wake County) and bill Medicaid under HCPCS H0019-TJ. Our program follows all state regulations, Medicaid requirements, and clinical best practices for residential treatment. We are actively preparing for CARF accreditation — the gold standard for behavioral health facilities.

Our home is in Wake County, North Carolina. For the safety and privacy of the children in our care, we share our street address during the referral and screening process rather than publishing it publicly. Children attend local community schools and participate in community activities — they are part of this community, supported and safe.

faqs.q: How do I start a referral?
faqs.a: You can submit a referral directly through our website at wellspringintervention.com/refer — the form is fully fillable online and submitted securely. Your referral is sent to our admissions team, who will review it within one business day and contact you to discuss next steps. If you prefer to call, our admissions line is staffed during business hours. Whether you are a referring professional, a DSS worker, or a parent exploring options — you are welcome here, and there is no obligation.

about.heading: Therapy, in the shape of a home.
about.body1: Well Spring Intervention is a licensed, staff-secure Level III residential treatment facility — a free-standing residential program licensed under 10A NCAC 27G .1700 — where children and adolescents receive intensive clinical care without leaving the warmth of a real home. Our program brings together individual therapy, group therapy, psychiatric medication management, behavioral treatment, and round-the-clock emotional support — woven into daily life so healing happens between sessions as much as during them. Per .1701(e), every child receives individualized supervision and structure of daily living, with services designed to minimize behaviors related to functional deficits, ensure safety, de-escalate out-of-control behaviors, assist with adaptive functioning, and support step-down to a less intensive setting. Every child has a primary licensed therapist, a Qualified Professional overseeing their treatment plan, and awake, trained professionals present around the clock.
about.body2: Located in Wake County, North Carolina, we serve young people ages 6–17 who have been placed out of home due to behavioral and mental health needs. Our program is intentionally small — four to six children in one household, well below the regulatory maximum of twelve permitted under .1706(a) — so every child receives deeply individualized clinical attention, and every licensed therapist, psychiatrist, and teacher has the time to truly know them. We are not an institution. We are a home where therapy lives in the ordinary moments — at the breakfast table, on the walk to school, over homework, and at bedtime — as much as in the therapy room.
